title: Ink Williams hears Burton solo; recording constantly
summary: Williams hears Burton play and sing alone for the first time, and they record steadily with Jimmy O'Brien leading the washboard band.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And that's the reason why they killed it on the market. And they had signed up for six parts to the thing. And they had them all rolled out and everything ready for it. Yeah. And I said, Mr. Melrose, you know what you're doing now. I said, won't this get us in trouble? I'll take care of all that. I said, okay. I said, I want to make money. It's true. I want to make all the money I can. So I went on down. And so, Hink Williams was standing back at the door when Jimmy Blythe was there with me. And that was the first time that Hink heard me play and sing by myself. And he thought about those ten years that he let go by then. Yeah. And he asked Jimmy, he says, whose number that is but his recording? He said, it's his own number. Why'd he get such stuff? He never let me have it. Yeah. And so then I was glad to hear him say that. So after recording, I told him, I said, that's some of the stuff I tried to get you to let me record years ago. Yeah. I says, you never had enough wax. See? I says, now Mr. Melrose sees where we can make some money out of this stuff. And we recorded, we was. We were recording every time it turned around. We were recording different numbers. So that was around my first experience of recording. And so all during this time, all recording, we'd have Johnny Dot breaking with his clarinet because Jimmy O'Brien then was the great lead for playing on the records with that washbowl band. And so every time we'd shoot Johnny Dot on it because he had a drawing card name too at that time. Yeah.
